ownership_decision.invariant: An agent's effective daily spend cap is the operator override when set, else the defined default; an override is in (0, 5000000] micros and survives re-registration.

boundary_decision.interaction: Operations keeps importing no other context. The agent loop in foundation reads the cap through the Journal port that operations implements, so the cap stays operations' fact.

domain_forces: A cap fixed at compile time cannot follow real spending without a redeploy.
A worker restart re-registers every definition and must not undo an operator's decision.
The gateway budget for a run must come from the same cap an operator sees.
implementation_design.decision: A nullable override column beside the defined default; the effective cap is computed in one query; the Journal port supplies it to the runner at every run start; the operator API refuses values outside (0, US$5] and audits from and to in the change's transaction.
invariants_preserved: Audit events are written in the same transaction as the change they record.
A run is budgeted against what the agent may still spend today.
rejected_alternatives: Overwriting the defined default: the next worker start would silently restore it.
An environment variable per agent: fixed at startup and invisible in the admin workbench.

record.statement: A platform agent's effective daily spend cap is the operator's override when one is set, otherwise the default its definition declares. An override must be above zero and at most US$5 a day, and re-registering the definitions replaces only the default, never the override.
examples: An operator raising an agent's cap to 5000000 micros takes effect at that agent's next run; 5000001 micros is refused.
Clearing the override returns the agent to the default its definition declares.
A worker restart re-registers every definition and the operator's override survives it.

approvals.scope: Operations rule: an agent's effective daily spend cap is the operator override when set, else the defined default, bounded to (0, US$5] and kept across re-registration
